title: How Steve Jobs framed the iPhone: fix what everyone hates, make complex tech easy to use
summary: Jobs explains why Apple built the iPhone: not from market research but because everyone hated their phones. He says Apple's core competence is making complex technology easy and self-discoverable, and at Macworld he lays out why fixed buttons give way to multitouch, plus the hardware-software integration behind it.

principles.text: Build what you and your friends actually want, not what market research or spreadsheets suggest.
principles.quote: And it wasn’t driven by a bunch of market research or financial spreadsheets about how big certain markets were. It wasn’t driven by that at all. It was driven by the fact that we all hated our phones.

principles.text: Features nobody can discover might as well not exist; make complex technology easy and self-discoverable.
principles.quote: And what our competence is, is making complex technology easy to use and self-discoverable.

principles.text: Aim to make a contribution by making something truly great that you love.
principles.quote: We thought we could make a contribution by making something truly great that we loved.

principles.text: Aim for a leapfrog product that is both smarter and easier, rather than trading one off against the other.
principles.quote: What we want to do is make a leapfrog product that is way smarter than any mobile device has ever been and super easy to use.

principles.text: Remove fixed controls so the interface can adapt to each application and to future ideas.
principles.quote: Well, every application wants a slightly different user interface, a slightly optimized set of buttons, just for it.

principles.text: Serious software people should make their own hardware; integrate the two.
principles.quote: “People who are really serious about software should make their own hardware.”
